ben.note: In game Ben is 33 px tall on a 0.8 by 2.0 tile body; the workshop frames pad him to 24 by 44.

walkIn.spriteRule: spriteX = exitX + spriteLeft; spriteY = (sill baseline + startBelowSill) - 36 (footLineRows) - rise[i]. Ben’s centre column 11 sits on the exit’s centre column 9.
walkIn.startBelowSill: game-defined: the floor line in front of the exit less the sill baseline

sidePass.note: Keyed doors are drawn before Ben, so Ben is in front of the whole door; he overlaps it only once it is open and passable.

keyedHeight.note: 3 tiles (16 × 48) is the standard door height. 2 tiles (16 × 32) is shown as a minimum only: Ben's body is exactly 32 px tall in the trial, so a 2-tile door fits him with no margin. The keyed door is a column of tiles, and the level decides how many.

keeps: top strip (the lintel and its lit top)
side face (the lit left jamb and the shaded right jamb)
heldOpen.note: The held open frame keeps the closed door's lintel strip and side faces as decoration. They are never solid: Ben is drawn in front of the whole door and nothing blocks him. The empty ending stays available.

night.litArt: The lift leaves, the shutter and every other door leaf and arch are ordinary lit art (bank 0): they dim with the scene at night.
night.glowLayer: Only the separate glow layer (the keyed badge, the exit's light and arrow) is drawn in the glow bank (bank 2, level 14) and stays at full brightness.

dosMemory.note: Red and blue are two stored copies, about 2.2 KB each at most, with identical grids (only the paint letters and the badge shape differ) so one colour-swapped copy stays possible later.

sound.dooropenMs: about 500, with a latch thud at the end
sound.status: Open decision for Scott: the `dooropen` sound is left as it is
sound.note: The openings here run 160 to 300 ms, shorter than the sound's 0.5 s, so the latch thud lands after the door has finished moving. Whether to retime the openings to the sound or cut the sound to 180 to 300 ms is Scott's call.

facts: The feet line is 16 px (one tile) below the exit's far-edge sill (`docs/OBLIQUE.md` in the Fizz 2 repo), so standing Ben's head is 17 px above the sill inside the 35 px arch, and the 7 px rise keeps it inside.
The walk-in's crop riding with Ben is accepted by Fizz 2: no raised lip is needed.
The keyed door is a column of tiles whose height the level decides.
The Fizz 2 session will write the importer, the front-layer pass after Ben, the door-opening presentation state and the walk-in.
Nothing is imported until Scott picks a keyed door, an exit and the ending.

drawOrder: Ground pass: back wall or sky, far-plane dressing, the exit (back, glow, then the front lip), terrain from the bottom row up with the keyed doors (back, then glow), spikes
New exit pass, only during the walk-in: the step's glowOver, then the exit's front lip again over Ben
At night, the light pass (the glow bank stays at full brightness)

designs.name: Plank Swing
designs.idea: A painted plank door in a stone case that swings away from you on its left hinge, foreshortening to its edge.
designs.why: The classic door: everyone reads a swing, the leaf narrows instead of moving, so it stays inside its 16 px column at any height.
notes: The badge squeezes with the leaf and is still a triangle or a disc at 8 px wide; at 4 px it is hidden and the plate goes dark.
The held open frame keeps the leaf edge against the left jamb, so the room remembers a door was here.

glow.draw: Drawn straight after the back layer at the same position, before Ben.

closed.note: Shut and locked: drawn in the ground pass with the terrain, before Ben.

opening.note: Plays once after the `dooropen` event. Presentation only: the door is already passable and Ben is drawn over it.

open.note: The held open frame: the doorway stays drawn for the rest of the room.

emptyEnding.note: The optional ending: after the opening frames the door is not drawn at all, as in Fizz 1.

designs.name: Pocket Slide
designs.idea: The leaf slides sideways into a slot in the right jamb, like a ship's pocket door.
designs.why: Pure sideways motion is the easiest opening to read at 16 px and needs no foreshortening; the slot says where it went.
notes: The badge rides with the leaf for the first step and is hidden once the jamb would cut it.
The held open frame leaves the leaf's edge showing in the slot.

designs.name: Twin Leaves
designs.idea: Two half leaves part from the middle under a fixed transom that carries the badge; the lock splits at the seam.
designs.why: The badge never moves, so the open doorway still says which key opened it; the split lock is a clear unlocked cue.
notes: The transom takes the top 11 rows of the top segment (the lintel, the badge plate and its underline). Under it the opening is 10 px wide between the jamb faces and 36 px tall on the standard 3-tile door, 4 px over the 32 px body of Ben; the 2-tile minimum leaves only 20 px, so a 2-tile Twin Leaves is tight and Ben passes in front of it rather than through a clear gap.
The badge is visible in every frame, open included.

designs.name: Lock Pop
designs.idea: The key turns the lock a quarter, the lock flashes white, then the whole leaf pops out of the frame in a ring of sparks.
designs.why: It puts the key's job on screen: the lock is what changes first, so the player sees cause and effect before the door goes.
notes: Only the bottom segment changes during the turn, so those frames cost one new 16 by 16 grid each.
The badge is visible until the pop.

designs.name: Fizz Dissolve
designs.idea: The leaf fizzes away from the floor up like a shaken soda, white bubbles at the edge, the badge plate the last thing left.
designs.why: It is the Fizz joke made into a door: on-brand, unlike any real door, and the bubbles hide the cost of the in-between frames.
notes: The plate holds until the last moment, so the badge is readable in every frame but the open one.
The dissolve is worked out per segment from the floor up, so it stacks to any height.

designs.name: Signpost Arch
designs.idea: An open stone arch with the badge on a sign hung from its head; while locked, iron bars in the door's colour fill it.
designs.why: The doorway itself never animates: one frame for the bars, one for the open arch, and the hanging sign keeps the badge in the room.
notes: No opening frames: the bars are gone on the `dooropen` tick, which the sound covers.
The sign hangs in the doorway; Ben is drawn over it as he walks through.

designs.name: Classic Block
designs.idea: Fizz 1's door tile grown into segments: a painted frame round brown grained boards, badge and lock; it simply vanishes.
designs.why: The cheapest and most faithful option: one frame, no open art, and it plays exactly as Fizz 1 did.
notes: There is no held open frame; the empty ending is the only ending.
The diagonal grain repeats every 4 rows, so stacked segments meet without a seam.

designs.name: Into the Light
designs.idea: An open stone arch full of green light; as Ben steps in, the light floods over him and fades back to an empty doorway.
designs.why: One doorway frame, and the walk-in is told by the light: two dither frames that glow at night with the rest of the exit, softening the crop.
notes: The veil is the glow layer drawn a second time after Ben (`glowOver`), at 6/16 and 12/16 coverage, then the full light, over the last three walk-in frames.

placement.note: The piece's top-left corner, relative to the exit cell's left edge and the top of the lower exit cell. Its bottom edge is the sill, on the far edge of the floor, higher on screen than the floor line Ben stands on in front of it.

glow.bank: GLOW: bank 2, level 14, left at full brightness by the night pass (`light.rs`)
glow.draw: Glow draws after the back layer and before Ben; a step's `glowOver` draws again after Ben, before the front lip.

idle.note: Waiting: back, glow and lip in the ground pass, before Ben.

enter.note: After the exit event: the walk-in, the light flooding over Ben, then fading with him gone.

designs.name: Over the Lip
designs.idea: The plain open arch: Ben walks in over the threshold lip and is gone.
designs.why: The cheapest exit that still shows Ben going in: the walk-in frames and the lip do all the work.
notes: The `ta-da!` sound carries the moment; nothing in the doorway moves.

placement.note: The piece's top-left corner, relative to the exit cell's left edge and the top of the lower exit cell. Its bottom edge is the sill, on the far edge of the floor, higher on screen than the floor line Ben stands on in front of it.

designs.name: Lighthouse Lift
designs.idea: A lift in the arch: the up arrow lights the transom, the steel leaves part when Ben presses Up and close once he is in.
designs.why: Press Up to go up: a lift explains the control by itself, and the closing leaves end the level with a clear beat.
notes: The leaves are on the back layer; the glow frame for each leaf frame is the light only where the leaves leave the cab open.
The transom is lower than the arch head; Ben's crown stays in front of it, since he never passes under it.

placement.note: The piece's top-left corner, relative to the exit cell's left edge and the top of the lower exit cell. Its bottom edge is the sill, on the far edge of the floor, higher on screen than the floor line Ben stands on in front of it.

glow.draw: Glow draws after the back layer and before Ben; a step's `glowOver` draws again after Ben, before the front lip.

idle.note: Shut, arrow lit: in the ground pass, before Ben.

opening.note: On the Up press, before the walk-in, with Ben frozen in front.

enter.note: The walk-in, then the leaves close.

designs.name: Drop Shutter
designs.idea: An open arch with an iron shutter hidden in its head; once Ben is in, it drops in three steps to the lip.
designs.why: The slam is a natural end-of-level beat, and the shut exit reads as spent if the camera lingers.
notes: The arch is always open while Ben plays; the shutter frames only follow the walk-in.
The shut shutter covers the arrow, so the shut frame has no glow.

designs.name: Lighthouse Door
designs.idea: A brown plank door in the arch with a round window over the arrow; it swings in on its left hinge and swings shut behind Ben.
designs.why: Matches the keyed doors' plank language, so exits and doors read as one family; the lit window keeps the arrow visible while shut.
notes: The leaf is on the back layer and the same three frames open and close; the glow follows the leaf, lighting only the window when shut.
